You lower yourself beside it and keep your hands still. The Teqqellon doesn't strike. Its outer membrane flexes under a skin-tight sheen, and the floating core inside gives a stronger pulse when your shadow crosses it.

You trace one finger along the edge of its shell-ridge. The surface fizzes faintly against your skin, then calms when you slow down. Fast pressure makes it tense. Slow pressure makes it part.
